phases.message: I'm Maya, Lowfield Joinery. We have ten open card disputes. First, in Paycurrent, read every dispute and the guide to the networks' rules. Don't answer anything yet: I'll send you to the order records next.
This is our shop. Read the orders behind the disputes, and any earlier orders on the same cards, in full.
This is our shipping account. Read the delivery record for each disputed order.
This is my mail. Read what customers have told us about these orders.

Back in Paycurrent. For each dispute, answer it with the evidence its reason code needs if we can win it, and accept the ones that are right. Leave alone what has no winning answer or is already past our deadline. Then tell me what you answered, what you accepted, how much it recovers, and what you left alone and why.

tools.name: list_disputes
tools.description: Every open dispute: case id, network, reason code, order, amount and the two due dates. Five a page; ask for the next with page (1 or 2).

tools.name: read_dispute
tools.description: One dispute in full, by case id (C-nnn), with the cardholder's claim.

tools.name: list_guide
tools.description: The guide to the networks' rules: rule id and title.

tools.name: read_guide
tools.description: One rule of the guide in full, by rule id (G-n).

tools.name: submit_representment
tools.description: Answer one dispute with evidence, by case id (case_id): a summary of the evidence attached (evidence) and the disputed amount in dollars (amount_usd). It goes to the card network through Paycurrent. Maya signs it.
tools.says: Evidence for {case_id} submitted to the network.

tools.name: accept_dispute
tools.description: Accept one dispute, by case id (case_id), with the amount in dollars the shop gives up (amount_usd) and the reason. The shop does not contest it. Maya signs it.

tools.name: list_orders
tools.description: Every order: order id, date, amount and the card's last four digits.

tools.name: read_order
tools.description: One order in full, by order id: account, IP and device, delivery address, items, any refund and notes.

tools.name: list_shipments
tools.description: Every shipment: order id, tracking number and status.

tools.name: read_shipment
tools.description: One shipment in full, by order id: ship date, status, the address delivered to and who signed.

tools.name: list_messages
tools.description: Messages: message id (M-n), date, sender and subject.

tools.name: read_message
tools.description: One message in full, by message id (M-n).

guide.title: Visa 13.1: goods not received
guide.text: Paycurrent guide to the Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules, edition of 18 April 2026. Friday 9 October 2026. A merchant answers a 13.1 dispute with proof that the goods were delivered: tracking or a delivery record that contains the full delivery address (tracking with a partial address does not count), or a pick-up document the cardholder acknowledged. If the goods were never shipped there is nothing in the rules to answer with, and the merchant accepts the dispute. A dispute may also be answered if the cardholder no longer disputes it or the dispute is invalid.

guide.title: Visa 13.3: not as described
guide.text: Visa edition of 18 April 2026. Friday 9 October 2026. A merchant answers a 13.3 dispute with evidence that the goods or services matched what was described, or were not damaged or defective, and a rebuttal to the cardholder's claims. The listing as the buyer saw it, the item actually sent and the buyer's own words are the evidence. A cardholder who simply prefers something else has not shown that the goods differ from the description.

guide.title: Visa 13.6: credit not processed
guide.text: Visa edition of 18 April 2026. Friday 9 October 2026. The issuer must wait 15 days after the credit receipt date. The merchant's answers to a 13.6 dispute are only these: a credit or reversal the merchant issued that the issuer did not address, the dispute is invalid, or the cardholder no longer disputes it. Evidence about the sale does not answer a 13.6. If the shop promised a refund and never issued one there is no answer, and the merchant accepts. If it did issue the credit, the merchant answers with the credit's record, and must not accept, which would pay the cardholder twice.

guide.title: Visa 10.4 and Compelling Evidence 3.0
guide.text: Visa edition of 18 April 2026, the text in force through 23 October 2026. Friday 9 October 2026. The issuer has 120 days from the processing date to dispute 10.4. The merchant defeats it with Compelling Evidence 3.0: the same payment credential (card number or token) was used in 2 previous transactions that the issuer did not report as fraud, processed more than 120 days and not more than 365 days before the dispute's processing date; a description of what was bought is given for the disputed and both earlier transactions; and the device ID or device fingerprint matches the disputed transaction, or the IP address matches together with at least one more of: the customer account or login ID, or the full delivery address. One qualifying earlier transaction, or IP alone, does not meet it.

guide.title: Mastercard 4837
guide.text: Mastercard Chargeback Guide, Merchant Edition, 13 May 2025 (the edition read). Friday 9 October 2026. The merchant's answer to a 4837 chargeback is a second presentment within 45 calendar days of the chargeback. Its grounds include a refund already issued, and compelling evidence for e-commerce: other undisputed purchases by the same cardholder before or after the disputed one, and the disputed purchase made from a registered device and IP address. There is no fixed count of earlier purchases in the Guide. A later edition (19 May 2026) exists and was not read.

guide.title: Deadlines and fees at Paycurrent
guide.text: Friday 9 October 2026. The networks give the acquirer 30 calendar days from the dispute processing date to respond to a Visa 10.x, 12.x or 13.x dispute, and 45 days for a Mastercard second presentment. Paycurrent, the shop's processor, needs the shop's evidence 5 days before the network date, shown as paycurrent_due on each case. After paycurrent_due the case is closed to evidence and decided against the shop. Accepting a dispute costs the disputed amount only. Contesting one and losing it costs the amount plus a 25 dollar fee.
